ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Text-embedding tuning for online adaptation of Grounding DINO
PROPOSAL: Adapt Grounding DINO with a Swin-T backbone online by updating only the text prompt embeddings of the class names, while every other weight stays frozen. For each incoming test batch, minimise the entropy of the region-to-text logits on boxes above a confidence threshold, and average the embeddings with an exponential moving average to keep them from drifting. Stream Cityscapes images through foggy and rainy variants, then COCO with synthetic corruptions, in a single pass with no access to source images or source statistics. Report mean average precision on each target stream together with the number of frames processed per second.
CONTROLS: Compare against the frozen zero-shot detector, against full-parameter self-training and against a closed-set test-time method built on Faster R-CNN. Repeat each stream with three random orderings of the images, and check zero-shot accuracy on a held-out category list after adaptation.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: We expect text-embedding tuning to add two to four points of mean average precision under fog and to cost almost nothing in speed. It could fail on streams where the target categories are absent from the prompt list, because entropy minimisation then has nothing useful to sharpen.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Normalisation-layer updating with a slowly moving teacher for open-set detection
PROPOSAL: Update only the affine parameters of the normalisation layers in a GLIP-T detector while it processes an unlabeled target stream. A teacher copy follows the student by an exponential moving average, produces pseudo-boxes on weakly augmented images, and the student learns from them on strongly augmented views. Draw the stream from Cityscapes under fog, from BDD100K at night, and from COCO with sensor noise. Never load source images or feature statistics from the source, and keep the label list as an open prompt so that new categories can appear. Measure mean average precision after each domain and the memory used by the adapted parameters.
CONTROLS: Compare against the frozen detector, against updating every weight and against a method that matches source feature statistics. Repeat with three seeds and compare a teacher with a fast decay against one with a slow decay.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: We expect gains of three to five mean average precision points on the night stream, and smaller ones on noise. The result fails if updating every weight gives a better score without losing zero-shot accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prototype memory for test images without usable pseudo-labels
PROPOSAL: Equip a Grounding DINO detector with a small memory of class prototypes that the adaptation loop fills from confident detections as the test stream proceeds. When an image yields no box above the confidence threshold, retrieve the nearest prototypes for each prompt category and convert them into soft targets for the decoder queries. The memory stores a fixed number of feature vectors per category and replaces the oldest first. Run on streams built from Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K and COCO with corruptions, and keep source data out of the loop entirely. Report mean average precision on all images and on the subset that had no confident box.
CONTROLS: Compare against dropping such images from the loss, against a lower fixed threshold and against the frozen detector. Run three seeds. Also measure how often retrieved prototypes come from the wrong category, since that is where the idea could break.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: We expect the largest gain on the subset with no confident boxes, perhaps four points of mean average precision, and a smaller overall gain. It fails if retrieval returns mostly wrong categories, which would push the detector toward its own errors.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Batch-adaptive confidence thresholds with an image-level fallback
PROPOSAL: Replace the fixed confidence cut-off of self-training with a threshold set for each test batch from the spread of detection scores, then give every image that still has no accepted box a weaker image-level target built from the average text-image similarity across its regions. Apply the method on top of Grounding DINO with a Swin-B backbone, adapting only the last decoder layers. Evaluate on a stream that moves from clear weather to fog to night in BDD100K, followed by COCO with corruptions, and use no source images at any point. Track mean average precision and the fraction of images without any pseudo-label.
CONTROLS: Compare against a fixed threshold at three levels, against the frozen model and against a rule that uses the same batch statistic but no fallback. Use three seeds, and report results by domain so that forgetting is visible.
COST: 350
PREDICTION: We expect fewer images without pseudo-labels, falling from about a fifth to under a twentieth, and a gain of two to three points. The approach fails if the image-level target adds noise that cancels the gain from the adaptive threshold.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Low-rank adapters on the fusion layers of a vision-language detector
PROPOSAL: Insert low-rank adapters into the cross-modal fusion layers and the text encoder of Grounding DINO and train them online on unlabeled target images, while the original weights stay frozen. A teacher produces pseudo-boxes and the adapters learn through a classification loss on those boxes and a consistency loss across two augmented views. Use ranks of four and sixteen. The test stream covers Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night images and COCO with weather corruptions. Do not store any source images or statistics. Report mean average precision, the number of trainable parameters and the speed in frames per second.
CONTROLS: Compare against the frozen model, against full fine-tuning and against adapters placed only in the image backbone. Repeat with three seeds and check zero-shot scores on a different benchmark after the stream ends.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: We expect fusion-layer adapters to recover most of the full fine-tuning gain with a small fraction of the parameters. The idea fails if adapters in the image backbone do as well, which would show that the language side plays little role.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Weak and strong view consistency for online vision-language detection
PROPOSAL: Build a mean-teacher loop around Grounding DINO. The teacher reads a lightly perturbed view of each test image and proposes boxes. The student reads a heavily perturbed view of the same image and learns to reproduce those boxes through a localisation and a classification loss. The student updates only its decoder and its text projection, and the teacher follows by an exponential moving average. Feed the loop with streams from Foggy Cityscapes and from BDD100K at night, and add a stream of COCO with blur and noise. Never read source images. Measure mean average precision, frames per second and the drop in zero-shot accuracy.
CONTROLS: Compare against the frozen detector, against a student trained without heavy perturbation and against a method that restores source statistics. Repeat with three seeds.
COST: 210
PREDICTION: We expect two to four points of mean average precision on the foggy and night streams, with at most one point lost in zero-shot accuracy. The method fails if the student drifts toward the teacher's mistakes on long streams.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anchoring region-text logits to preserve zero-shot knowledge
PROPOSAL: Adapt GLIP-L online with a self-training loss plus a regulariser that keeps the region-to-text logits of the adapted model close to those of a frozen copy on the same test images. The regulariser uses a Kullback-Leibler divergence weighted by the confidence of the frozen copy. Update the decoder and the final fusion layer only. Run on Cityscapes with fog, BDD100K at night, and COCO with corruptions, and add an unseen vocabulary of rare categories to the prompt list so that cross-category behaviour appears. Report mean average precision on the target stream and on rare categories, and forgetting after the stream ends.
CONTROLS: Compare against self-training without the regulariser, against the frozen model and against a fixed small learning rate. Repeat with three seeds, and vary the regulariser weight over a short range.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: We expect the regulariser to cut forgetting on rare categories by half while keeping most of the gain on the target stream. It fails if the best regulariser weight erases the gain from adaptation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pseudo-label scarcity under confidence filtering in test-time detection
PROPOSAL: Measure how often images lose all pseudo-labels when a Grounding DINO detector filters boxes by confidence, and then test a repair. Count, for thresholds from 0.2 to 0.6, the share of images without an accepted box on Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO with corruptions. Next, give such images a replacement target made from the highest scoring box per prompt category, down-weighted in the loss. Adapt the decoder only, with an exponential moving average teacher and no source data. Report the empty share, mean average precision and the frames per second.
CONTROLS: Compare against a loss that skips empty images, against lowering the threshold and against the frozen model. Run three seeds and report per-domain results.
COST: 140
PREDICTION: We expect between a tenth and a third of images to lack pseudo-labels at the usual threshold, and the replacement target to give about two points. The repair fails if its targets are wrong too often to help.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continual stream of corruptions to test forgetting in adapted detectors
PROPOSAL: Evaluate a Grounding DINO detector that adapts through low-rank adapters while the domain changes every few thousand images, in the order clear, fog, rain, night, snow and back to clear. Use BDD100K and Cityscapes variants and COCO corruptions for category variety. After each switch, measure mean average precision on the current domain and on all previous domains, and compute average forgetting. The adaptation uses pseudo-labels from an exponential moving average teacher, and keeps source data out of reach throughout.
CONTROLS: Compare against the frozen model, against resetting the adapters at every switch and against a single pass of adaptation on the mixed stream. Run three seeds with different domain orders.
COST: 230
PREDICTION: Continual adaptation should beat resetting on late domains by a few points, at the price of some forgetting on early ones. It fails if forgetting grows with the stream length until the model falls under the frozen one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sparse parameter selection for real-time adaptation of a vision-language detector
PROPOSAL: Choose a few percent of the parameters of Grounding DINO for online updates by ranking them with the gradient of the entropy loss on the first hundred test images of each domain, then freeze the rest. Update the chosen parameters with pseudo-labels from a teacher, and compare their placement across the backbone, fusion layers and decoder. Test on Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO with corruptions. Report mean average precision, the latency per frame, and peak memory, and keep source images out of the procedure.
CONTROLS: Compare against random selection of the same number of parameters, against updating the normalisation layers only and against the frozen model. Repeat with three seeds.
COST: 55
PREDICTION: We expect gradient-selected parameters to match full adaptation within a point while keeping latency near the frozen model. It fails if random selection performs as well, which would make the ranking step pointless.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online prompt and normalisation tuning of Grounding DINO under fog and night shifts
PROPOSAL: Adapt Grounding DINO with a Swin-T backbone online by updating the text prompt embeddings and the affine parameters of the normalisation layers on pseudo-boxes from an exponential moving average teacher, without reading source images or source statistics. Stream Foggy Cityscapes, then BDD100K night images, then COCO with synthetic corruptions, in a single pass at 800-pixel short side. Report mean average precision on each stream and frames per second.
CONTROLS: Compare against the frozen zero-shot detector and against full-parameter self-training, with the stream order held fixed. Compare against a closed-set test-time method built on Faster R-CNN, with the label list restricted to source categories. Repeat the stream with three random orders and three seeds each. Compare the adapted prompt embeddings frozen against the same embeddings updated.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: We expect three to five points of mean average precision on the night stream relative to the frozen detector, at a small cost in speed. The claim fails if full-parameter self-training scores higher than prompt and normalisation tuning on every stream.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-time adaptation of GLIP-T with a moving-average teacher and confident boxes
PROPOSAL: Update GLIP-T online with a teacher whose weights track the student by exponential moving average, using boxes above a confidence of 0.4 as targets and touching the decoder layers and the language projection only. The stream goes from Cityscapes under rain to BDD100K dusk images and then to COCO with noise, processed once at 800-pixel short side. Source images and source feature statistics stay out of the loop. Report mean average precision on each stream and frames per second.
CONTROLS: Compare against the Faster R-CNN detector supervised on source labels and against fully supervised training on target labels, with the stream order held fixed. Compare against an offline adaptation method that reads source images, with the label list restricted to source categories. Repeat the stream with three random orders and three seeds each. Compare the backbone small against the same backbone large.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: We expect two to four points of mean average precision on the dusk stream relative to the zero-shot detector, at a small cost in speed. The claim fails if the supervised detector scores higher than the adapted one on every stream.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Which parts of a vision-language detector to update at test time
PROPOSAL: Find out which of updating the text side, the vision side or both gives the best online adaptation of Grounding DINO with a Swin-T backbone. A teacher copy follows the student by exponential moving average and proposes pseudo-boxes above a confidence of 0.3 for every group of 8 images. Use streams from Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO with weather corruptions, and keep source images out. Report mean average precision after each stream and the share of parameters that changed.
CONTROLS: Compare updating the text side alone against updating the vision side alone and both together, with the pseudo-label rule held fixed. Compare a teacher decay of 0.99 against 0.999, with the stream order repeated. Compare a low confidence cut-off against a high one, with seeds repeated. Compare the adapted model against the frozen one on every stream.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Updating both sides should add about one point over the best single side on the night stream. The idea fails if one side alone reaches the same score within seed variation on every stream.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Engineering factors in online adaptation of a vision-language detector
PROPOSAL: Run online adaptation of Grounding DINO with a Swin-T backbone, with the decoder updated from pseudo-boxes above a confidence of 0.3 proposed by an exponential moving average teacher, and ask how engineering choices around that loop change the outcome. Use streams from Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO with weather corruptions, and keep source images out. Report mean average precision after each stream and the wall-clock speed in frames per second.
CONTROLS: Compare an image short side of 640 against 800, with the pseudo-label rule held fixed. Compare mixed precision against full precision, with the stream order repeated. Compare loader worker counts of 2 against 8, with seeds repeated. Compare the adapted model against the frozen one on every stream.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Mixed precision should leave mean average precision within a fraction of a point while raising speed. The idea fails if the engineering choices move the score by more than seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-category online adaptation of a vision-language detector under weather shift
PROPOSAL: Adapt Grounding DINO with a Swin-B backbone online on unlabeled target streams whose categories partly differ from the source: Foggy Cityscapes with an added list of rare road objects, BDD100K night with extra vehicle types, and COCO corruptions with novel animal names in the prompts. A moving-average teacher supplies pseudo-boxes above a confidence of 0.35 and the student updates normalisation and prompt parameters. Source data stays untouched at every point. Report mean average precision on seen and on added categories.
CONTROLS: Compare the adapted model against the frozen detector on each shifted stream, with the prompt list held fixed. Compare seen against added categories on the same images, with seeds repeated. Compare a stream whose prompts include categories absent from the images against one whose prompts match them. Compare adaptation speed in frames per second against the frozen model.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Added categories should gain less than seen ones, perhaps one point against three. The claim fails if the adapted model loses accuracy on the added categories.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online adaptation of a vision-language detector on clean in-distribution streams
PROPOSAL: Apply online adaptation to Grounding DINO with a Swin-B backbone on streams that match the data it was trained on, namely clean COCO validation photographs, ordinary Cityscapes frames and BDD100K daytime clips showing common vehicle classes. A moving-average teacher supplies pseudo-boxes above a confidence of 0.35 and the student updates normalisation and prompt parameters. Keep source data out of reach at every point. Report mean average precision on each stream and the confidence histogram.
CONTROLS: Compare the adapted model against the frozen detector on each clean stream, with the prompt list held fixed. Compare common against rare categories on the same images, with seeds repeated. Compare a stream whose prompts include categories absent from the images against one whose prompts match them. Compare adaptation speed in frames per second against the frozen model.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Rare categories should gain less than common ones, perhaps one point against three. The claim fails if the adapted model loses accuracy on the rare categories.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Judging adaptation quality of Grounding DINO by target detection accuracy
PROPOSAL: Adapt Grounding DINO with a Swin-T backbone online with a teacher-student loop, in which a moving-average teacher proposes boxes above a confidence of 0.4 and the student updates its decoder. Stream Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO with corruptions. Because target labels exist for evaluation only, measure the quality of adaptation by the mean average precision of the final model on each stream against its annotations, together with the average precision at a loose overlap level.
CONTROLS: Report mean average precision and the loose-overlap average precision of the adapted and frozen models on each stream, with the stream order held fixed. Report the same two scores on a shuffled stream order, with seeds repeated. Report the per-category score, matched by instance count. Report the speed in frames per second after the stream ends.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Detection accuracy should rise by about three points on the night stream and by less elsewhere. The idea fails if the final scores stay inside seed variation of the frozen model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Judging adaptation quality of Grounding DINO by internal confidence statistics
PROPOSAL: Run an online teacher-student loop on Grounding DINO with a Swin-T backbone, where a moving-average teacher proposes boxes above a confidence of 0.4 and the student updates its decoder. Stream Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO with corruptions. Since the point is to see the model's own state, follow the mean confidence of accepted boxes on each stream, along with the share of images with at least one accepted box.
CONTROLS: Report mean confidence and the share of accepted boxes of the adapted and frozen models on each stream, with the stream order held fixed. Report the same two quantities on a shuffled stream order, with seeds repeated. Report the per-category entropy, matched by instance count. Report the speed in frames per second after the stream ends.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Mean confidence should rise by about three points on the night stream and by less elsewhere. The idea fails if the final statistics stay inside seed variation of the frozen model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rescuing test images that lack confident pseudo-labels in online detection adaptation
PROPOSAL: Adapt GLIP-L online with a moving-average teacher, and give every image that lacks a box above a confidence of 0.5 a fallback target: the nearest class prototypes stored from earlier confident boxes, with a soft loss on the decoder queries. Draw the stream from Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO with corruptions, never reading source images. Evaluate mean average precision on all images and separately on images that lacked a confident box.
CONTROLS: Compare the fallback against skipping images that lack a confident box, on the images that lacked pseudo-labels, with the stream held fixed. Compare a fixed lower threshold of 0.3 against the fallback, with seeds repeated. Compare the adapted model against the frozen one on the full stream. Compare a prototype bank of 8 against 32 vectors per category.
COST: 560
PREDICTION: The largest gain should sit on images without confident boxes, about four points. The study fails if skipping those images reaches the same score within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Loss reweighting of images with abundant pseudo-labels in online detector adaptation
PROPOSAL: Run GLIP-L online with a teacher that trails the student, and for images where the teacher accepts at least five boxes above a confidence of 0.5, raise the loss weight with the number of accepted boxes through a monotone rule. The streams are Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO corruptions, with source images off-limits. Score mean average precision over all images, and again on the images with abundant boxes only.
CONTROLS: Compare down-weighting images with abundant boxes against leaving their weight untouched, on those images, with the stream held fixed. Compare a stricter cut-off of 0.7 against the reweighting, with seeds repeated. Compare the adapted model against the frozen one on the full stream. Compare weight growth of 8 against 32 steps per accepted box.
COST: 560
PREDICTION: Images with abundant boxes should gain about four points, while the full stream gains less. The study fails if leaving their weight untouched reaches the same score within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt and normalisation tuning of a vision-language detector on an unlabeled stream
PROPOSAL: Adapt Grounding DINO online to Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO corruptions without source images or statistics. A moving-average teacher proposes boxes above a confidence of 0.4 for each test batch, and the student updates the text prompt embeddings and the normalisation layers only, which keeps the pre-trained weights close to their starting point. Add an entropy term on the logits of images with no confident box. Evaluate mean average precision on seen and unseen categories and frames per second.
CONTROLS: Compare against the frozen detector and full-parameter self-training. Run three seeds and three stream orders.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The adapted model should gain three to four points on the night stream and keep most zero-shot accuracy. The direction fails if full self-training wins on all streams.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Descriptive class prompts written by a language model for zero-shot detection
PROPOSAL: Improve Grounding DINO on Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO corruptions by replacing each class name with a longer description generated once by a language model, such as the typical look of the object in fog or low light, and by averaging scores over several descriptions. Keep every detector weight frozen. Add a calibration of score thresholds per domain from a handful of labeled target images. Evaluate mean average precision on seen and unseen categories and frames per second.
CONTROLS: Compare against the plain class names and one hand-written description per class. Run three seeds and three description sets.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Descriptive prompts should gain two to three points on the night stream and keep zero-shot accuracy. The direction fails if plain names do as well on all streams.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prototype memory for images lacking confident pseudo-labels at test time
PROPOSAL: Add a class prototype memory to GLIP-L online adaptation. When an image has no box above the confidence cut-off, retrieve the prototypes of each prompt category from the memory and turn them into soft decoder targets with a lowered weight. Prototypes are filled from confident detections as the stream goes on, and replaced oldest first. Run on streams from Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO corruptions without source data. Report mean average precision on all images and on images lacking confident boxes.
CONTROLS: Compare against skipping such images and a lower cut-off. Run three seeds and three stream orders.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: Images without confident boxes should gain around four points, and the overall score two. The direction fails if retrieval returns many wrong categories.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Restoration front-end that removes fog and noise before detection
PROPOSAL: Place an image restoration network in front of Grounding DINO that removes fog, rain streaks and sensor noise, trained once on paired clean and degraded frames from Cityscapes. The restored frames pass to the frozen detector with unchanged weights and prompts. Evaluate on Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO with corruptions, reporting mean average precision on all images and on images with heavy degradation, and the added time per frame.
CONTROLS: Compare against the detector on raw frames and a simple contrast stretch. Run three seeds and three degradation levels.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: Heavily degraded images should gain around four points, and the overall score two. The direction fails if restoration introduces artefacts that hurt detection.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adapters with a slowly moving teacher for preserved zero-shot knowledge
PROPOSAL: Insert low-rank adapters into the fusion layers of Grounding DINO and train them online with pseudo-boxes from a moving-average teacher, keeping the original weights untouched. Use a consistency loss between two perturbed views and a distance penalty to the frozen logits on categories absent from the images. Test on Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO corruptions without source images, with a prompt list that includes rare categories. Report mean average precision on target and rare categories, the change in zero-shot accuracy, and frames per second.
CONTROLS: Compare against the frozen model and full fine-tuning. Run three seeds with adapter ranks of 4 and 16.
COST: 410
PREDICTION: Adapters should recover most of the full fine-tuning gain with little forgetting. The direction fails if forgetting on rare categories matches full fine-tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large supervised multi-domain fine-tuning of a vision-language detector
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Grounding DINO offline on a large pooled set with box labels drawn from Cityscapes, BDD100K and COCO, covering fog, night and many other conditions, using a long schedule and strong augmentation. The final weights then stay fixed at deployment. Test on held-out Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO corruption images, with a prompt list that includes rare categories. Report mean average precision on target and rare categories, the change in zero-shot accuracy, and frames per second.
CONTROLS: Compare against the zero-shot model and a shorter schedule. Run three seeds with pooled set fractions of one half and the whole.
COST: 410
PREDICTION: Pooled fine-tuning should add a few points on seen conditions with some zero-shot loss. The direction fails if rare categories lose as much as the gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Batch-adaptive confidence thresholds with an image-level fallback target
PROPOSAL: Set the pseudo-label threshold for each test batch from the spread of detection scores, and give images with no accepted box a weak image-level target built from average text-region similarity. Apply this to Grounding DINO with a Swin-B backbone, adapting the last decoder layers only. Use a stream that goes from clear weather to fog to night in BDD100K, then COCO with corruptions, without source images. Report mean average precision and the share of images lacking any pseudo-label.
CONTROLS: Compare against fixed thresholds and the frozen model. Run three seeds and three stream orders.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The share of images lacking pseudo-labels should fall sharply and accuracy should gain two to three points. The direction fails if the fallback adds noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a vision-language detector into a compact student for fast inference
PROPOSAL: Train a compact student detector with a ResNet-50 backbone to mimic the box and text-aligned class outputs of Grounding DINO on a pool of unlabeled driving images, aiming at low latency on embedded hardware. The student keeps a fixed prompt list for deployment. Evaluate on Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO corruptions, reporting mean average precision, latency per frame, and the share of teacher accuracy retained.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher and a student trained on labels. Run three seeds and three pool fractions.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The student should retain most of the teacher accuracy at a fraction of the latency. The direction fails if accuracy falls sharply on night images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online estimation of target feature statistics without source data
PROPOSAL: Replace the source-derived statistics used by earlier test-time detection methods with running estimates of feature mean and variance computed from the target stream itself, and use them to align features of Grounding DINO online. Combine the alignment with a moving-average teacher whose pseudo-boxes pass a confidence filter. Evaluate on Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO corruptions without any source image. Report mean average precision, forgetting on prompt categories, and frames per second.
CONTROLS: Compare against methods using source statistics, and the frozen model. Run three seeds and three stream orders.
COST: 275
PREDICTION: Target-only statistics should match source statistics within a point. The direction fails if early batches give unstable estimates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Test-time augmentation and score voting for a frozen vision-language detector
PROPOSAL: Run Grounding DINO frozen on each test image under several scales and flips, merge the boxes with weighted box fusion, and vote on class scores across views. No weights change during testing. Take the views from three scales and a horizontal flip, and weight each view by its mean detection score. Evaluate on Foggy Cityscapes, BDD100K night and COCO corruptions, and report mean average precision, accuracy on rare prompt categories, and frames per second, since every view adds forward passes.
CONTROLS: Compare against single-view inference and non-maximum suppression. Run three seeds and three view sets.
COST: 275
PREDICTION: Voting should add about two points on blurry images at several times the cost per frame. The direction fails if single-view inference stays close.
